question: Walking at (3)/(4)th of his normal speed from his home, Manish is 8 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed becomes 3/4 ⇒ Time becomes 4/3

Extra time = (4/3 − 1) = 1/3 of normal time

(1/3) × T = 8 ⇒ T = 24

**∴ Answer = 24 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduced speed = 3/4 of normal speed

Delay = 8 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time ∝ 1 / Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let normal time = T

⇒ New time = T × (4/3)

⇒ Delay = New time − Normal time

⇒ T × (4/3) − T = 8

⇒ T(4/3 − 1) = 8

⇒ T × (1/3) = 8

⇒ T = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

Time is inversely proportional to speed for fixed distance

Ratio Concept

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a

Delay Formula

Delay = New time − Original time

Shortcut Insight

Extra time fraction directly helps find original time
